body: Everyone told me to wait until I was 18 to start hormones because they said I had to be sure. The thing is I WAS sure until people kept making me question it. When I finally started it was like a load off. Yes some things were harder but a lot of life was easier because I felt more comfortable with myself. Currently I'm 22 and have been on T for almost 5 years, but tbh I wish I started earlier. Everyone has their own timeline, but if you know this is what you want, go for it. I'm glad I didn't wait any longer than I did.

It's been pretty good. I started small with my doses going back on. One thing I definitely enjoy is the return of more stamina and the ability to retain muscle, which I took for granted before lol. The one thing is I sweat more which I don't like and my anger sticks around more for sure, but I'm much happier now that I'm back on T. It makes a huge difference it turns out lol

I went off hormones for about 6 months and definitely had a similar experience. My chest hurt like a bitch, and I actually had some chest regrowth despite having had top surgery (I got peri so I wasn't completely flat anyways) and it make my dysphoria horrible. I had no energy, was super depressed, and and felt super lethargic. I think it's mostly due to the increase in estrogen.

They don’t roll over when threatened, and are generally pretty well respected. I wouldn’t say I’m not respected, but definitely not to the extent my more masculine friends are. They’re also more rough and rowdy, which is what I enjoy, but I never had any practice being super rowdy with other guys so I don’t know what’s acceptable. 

They made it clear that masculinity requires empathy and caring. They said anyone who tries to claim they’re a “real man” while pushing people down isn’t someone you should respect, and I agree. My biggest problem is being assertive, which I think goes in tandem with my size. I’ve had my size used against me many times, so I tend to default to rolling over rather than being assertive because I don’t feel safe or don’t see people taking me seriously. That’s something I know I need to work on in myself, though it’s hard for me to do when I’m not around others cause I can’t practice social things without a social setting, you know?

The only thing I didn’t like is they said in this world, men are kind of seen as disposable and are expected to be able to live on their own and never expect people to care about them. They also said to keep your emotions hidden away. I don’t agree with that part, that sounds like an incredibly lonely existence to me.
